description: Attack n=352 B=40 (~1612us) — the largest tiny/medium shape and NEITHER existing kernel's strength. The 352x352 FP32 matrix (495KB) overruns the single-CTA 227KB SMEM cap, so the fused whole-matrix megakernel can't apply and it currently runs the large-n-oriented blocked panel+cuBLAS path. Build a path that fits: either a 2-pass / panel-resident SMEM megakernel (only the active NB-wide panel + the WMMA trailing tiles live in SMEM; the trailing block is loaded incrementally from global, like the n=512/1024 fused megakernel does) processing one matrix per CTA, OR a multi-CTA-tiled cooperative factorization splitting the 352 rows across CTAs. Both make the 40-matrix batch (SM-rich) factor concurrently in one launch, killing the per-panel cuBLAS launch storm. Keep all other n exactly as parent. FP32 panel (TF32 panel fails the gate); avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Fully-fused n=352 megakernel (1 CTA/matrix, NB-wide panel in SMEM, trailing block updated in-place in global, CB=32 T=256). Validate PASS + all 3 guards CLEAN. REGRESSION: n=352 1617->4192us, geomean 4859->5287us. nsys: the fused kernel is 100pct of time (8.9ms/launch x13), 0.27 waves (40 CTAs/148 SMs). The trailing update -- bulk of FLOPs -- now runs SERIALLY inside 40 starved CTAs instead of cuBLAS full-batch tensor-friendly tiling, which dominates the loss. Fusing the launch storm helped the panel but moving trailing off cuBLAS hurt more. Next: keep fused panel + route trailing GEMM back to cuBLAS bmm (hybrid), or multi-CTA cooperative to raise occupancy.

Fused n=352 megakernel, threads 256->512 (CB=32, only knob change). REGRESSION: n=352 4192->7999us, geomean 11069us (n>=512 shapes measured noisy-high this run too, likely transient). The wider 512-thread CTA hurts the serial panel recurrence under register pressure with only 40 CTAs. Confirms the single-CTA fused structure is occupancy-bound; bigger CTAs do not help. Pivoting to multi-CTA cooperative (G CTAs/matrix, split trailing cols) to fill SMs.

Route n=352 to _routed_qr: cb=16->32 + TF32-well/FP32-ill trailing GEMM (was FP32 SIMT). Validate PASS, all 3 guards CLEAN (n=352 test factor residual 8.17<20 gate; diff-guard case-rotation OK -> TF32 routing correct at n=352). NEUTRAL: n=352 1617->1662us, geomean 4874us. TF32 trailing does NOT help here: at B=40 the trailing GEMM is launch-bound not compute-bound; the classifier + n_well .item() host-sync adds cost. Panel factorization (73.6pct of n=352 profile) is the dominant serial cost -- that is the lever. Next: fuse the 22 panel launches into fewer/one, OR multi-CTA cooperative panel.

Multi-CTA cooperative cluster kernel: G=4 CTAs/matrix, cb=32, replicated FP32 panel + distributed trailing (CTA cr owns trailing cols [tj+cr::G]), 1 cluster.sync/panel. Thread-block clusters WORK and FP32 quality is excellent (n=352 test factor residual 0.0185, vs 8.17 for the TF32 path). Validate PASS + all 3 guards CLEAN. REGRESSION: n=352 1617->7860us, geomean 5542us. Causes: (1) 4x redundant full-panel factorization across the cluster, (2) the distributed trailing update is done one-column-at-a-time with 3 __syncthreads per column -- serial and sync-heavy. Cluster STRUCTURE is correct; the trailing-update implementation is naive. Next: batch the trailing columns into tiles (amortize syncs), reduce panel redundancy.

Cluster kernel trailing update -> COALESCED + TILED: each CTA owns a contiguous trailing column-block, sweeps it TC=32 cols at a time, stages W=V^T C and Y=T^T W in SMEM with consecutive threads owning consecutive columns so the global C reads/writes coalesce (was a per-column stride-n sweep). n=352 7860->4210us (1.87x within the cluster line). Validate PASS + all 3 guards CLEAN, FP32 quality (factor residual 0.0185). geomean 5265us, still > parent 4859 (n=352 4210 vs 1617). The 4x-redundant FP32 panel across G=4 CTAs is now the dominant cost. Next: de-replicate panel (DSMEM row-split) or reduce G.

Cluster (CB,G) structured sweep at n=352: CB=16/G=8 -> 3850us, CB=32/G=4 -> 4210us, CB=16/G=2 -> 12703us. G=8 best (320 CTAs + trailing split 8 ways); G=2 worst (trailing only halved -> long serial per-CTA column chunks). Settled CB=16/G=8, geomean 5228us. Validate PASS + 3 guards CLEAN. ncu (trial5, G=4): occupancy 7.1pct / 0.36 waves -- 107 reg/thread + large SMEM + cluster co-residency limit blocks/SM, and the REDUNDANT panel makes all G CTAs stall in lockstep at the same barriers (zero latency hiding). The redundant-panel cluster does NOT beat parent 1617us. Open: DSMEM row-split panel (genuinely different work per CTA to hide the barrier latency) is the untried completion of brief option 2.

De-replicate the cluster panel: CTA 0 factors panel + builds T, other CTAs read V/T from CTA-0 SMEM via DSMEM (cluster.map_shared_rank) for the distributed trailing. Validate PASS + 3 guards CLEAN -> DSMEM cross-CTA SMEM read is correct (n=352 residual 0.0176). REGRESSION: n=352 3850->6775us, geomean 5474us. Root cause measured: with CTA-0-only panel, G-1=7 of every G=8 cluster CTAs sit IDLE through the dominant panel phase and only 40 CTAs run during it (vs 320 when the panel was replicated). So the 'redundant' panel was providing latency hiding. The actual unlock is a row-SPLIT panel (all G CTAs do DIFFERENT rows, busy + non-redundant) with DSMEM cross-CTA reductions per column -- the heavy-sync completion of brief option 2, still untried.

Parent blocked panel + cuBLAS FP32 trailing, panel launched gdup=8 CTAs/matrix (320 redundant panel CTAs as occupancy filler; trailing stays on cuBLAS). GDUP templated -> n!=352 byte-identical (shapes 0/1/3 unchanged: 32.9/556.9/8732us). Validate PASS + 3 guards CLEAN (FP32 residual 0.0176). REGRESSION: n=352 1617->1936us, geomean 4931us. Measured disproof of the redundant-panel-occupancy idea: extra CTAs queue (panel SMEM caps co-residency ~4 blocks/SM) and add 8x global-write traffic + redundant compute, while the serial Householder dependency chain length is unchanged -> no net latency hiding. Sweeping gdup=2 next; if also >parent, the redundant-replica lever is exhausted and the row-SPLIT panel (different work/CTA) is the remaining option-2 variant.

gdup sweep: gdup=2 -> n=352 1614.7us (TIED parent 1617, within run noise), gdup=8 -> 1936us (worse). geomean 4861.7us (parent 4859.7, tied). The redundant-replica panel occupancy-filler caps at parity with the parent and never beats it -- the serial Householder per-column dependency chain at B=40 is the true limiter and redundant CTAs cannot shorten it. Settled gdup=2 (neutral, harmless). Open option-2 variant not yet built: TRUE row-SPLIT panel (each cluster CTA owns DIFFERENT rows, cross-CTA DSMEM reductions per column) -- the only path that shortens per-CTA reduction work, at the cost of ~2 cluster.sync/column.

n=352 panel CTA threads 128->256 (gdup=1, cb=16, cuBLAS FP32 trailing kept). The 256-thread CTA halves the tall per-column reduction (m<=352 rows) and gives 8 warps/CTA vs 4 to hide the serial-recurrence barrier latency on the same 40 CTAs. n!=352 byte-identical (512-thread n=2048 path untouched). Validate PASS + 3 guards CLEAN (FP32 residual 0.0188). SMALL clean WIN: n=352 1617->1580.6us, geomean 4859.7->4850.6us (~0.2pct). [A contended-GPU bench had read 3217us/10250 -- INVALID, shapes 3/6 showed 21k/112k vs known 8.7k/52k; clean re-run authoritative.] Open: sweep gdup x 256-threads; profile to see if reduction or barrier now dominates the 256-thread panel.

n=352 panel cb 16->32 + threads=256 (gdup=1, cuBLAS FP32 trailing kept). cb=32 halves the panel count (11 vs 22) -> half the panel-kernel launches AND half the cuBLAS trailing-GEMM launches; 256 threads keep the per-panel reductions fast over the wider cb. Validate PASS + 3 guards CLEAN (FP32 residual 0.0177). CLEAN WIN (shape3=8728 == parent, no contention): n=352 1617->1529us (-5.4pct on shape), geomean 4859.7->4834.8us = 1.0051x. [An earlier cb=32 read of 3177us/10250 geomean was fleet contention (shape3 21k vs known 8.7k); the clean re-run is authoritative.] This is the productive direction: stay on parent structure (custom panel + cuBLAS trailing), tune the panel. Open: gdup x (cb=32,256-threads); cb=24; profile the cb=32/256 panel.

n=352 panel __launch_bounds__ minBlocks 1->2 (MINB template; cb=32/threads=256/gdup=1). Tests whether the parent (.,1) bound pinned the under-occupied panel to 1 block/SM. n!=352 keep MINB=1 (byte-identical). Validate PASS + 3 guards CLEAN. MEASURED TIE (clean, shape3=8740): n=352 1530us, geomean 4836us=1.0048x (MINB=1 was 1529/4835, within noise). Confirms the n=352 panel is latency-bound by the serial Householder column chain at B=40, NOT co-residency-limited -- occupancy hints (MINB, gdup-replication, threads>256) do not help. cb=32+threads=256 is the practical optimum of the parent (custom panel + cuBLAS trailing) structure, giving the run's best n=352=1529us / geomean 4835us / 1.005x.

ROW-SPLIT cooperative cluster kernel (qr_cluster_rs_kernel): G CTAs/matrix factor the panel with rows distributed (r%G==cr), cross-CTA DSMEM reductions per Householder column (~2 cluster.sync/col, ~700-1000 total over 11 panels), distributed coalesced trailing. BUILT clean. HUNG at validate: ran >30min GPU-bound with zero progress (eval.py test stuck), had to kill it. Root cause: under the fleet's heavy concurrent GPU load (both B200s ~100pct from sibling briefs) a thread-block cluster cannot gang-schedule all G member CTAs co-resident, so the per-column cluster.sync blocks indefinitely -- the known cluster requirement that all member CTAs be simultaneously resident is unsatisfiable at low occupancy + contention. This is the row-split (option-2) variant; it needs either a contention-free GPU, far fewer cluster.syncs (batch all per-column reductions), or a non-cluster cross-CTA scheme (grid-stride + global atomics). Removed the hanging kernel; n=352 reverted to the proven blocked path.

FINAL cleaned state: n=352 on the proven blocked path (custom FP32 panel cb=32 + threads=256 + gdup=1 + launch-bounds MINB=2; cuBLAS FP32 trailing), hanging row-split kernel removed. Validate PASS + 3 guards CLEAN (n=352 factor residual 0.0177, FP32 quality). Clean bench (shape3=8774 confirms no contention): n=352 1531us (parent 1617, -5.3pct on shape), geomean 4850us = 1.002x over parent. This is the run's best n=352 result. The win is from the parent-structure panel tuning (cb 16->32 halves panel+trailing launch count; 256-thread CTA shortens the tall per-column reductions). All structural rewrites (fused single-CTA in-kernel trailing; multi-CTA clusters: replicated/CTA-0-DSMEM/row-split) regressed or hung -- see prior trials.

n=352 B=40 explored over 14 trials. BEST: parent-structure custom FP32 panel + cuBLAS FP32 trailing, with the panel TUNED (cb 16->32 + threads 128->256, gdup=1): n=352 1617->1529-1531us (-5.3pct), geomean 4860->4835us (trial 10, commit 01c41008, 1.0051x; HEAD 9c1670db is the cleaned tied state 4850us/1.002x with the hanging row-split kernel removed). cb=32 halves the panel+trailing launch COUNT (22->11 panels); 256-thread CTA shortens the tall per-column reductions (m<=352). All n!=352 kept BYTE-IDENTICAL (GDUP/MINB templated so gdup=1 path is unchanged; 512-thread n=2048 untouched). Validate PASS + all 3 guards CLEAN every trial; FP32 throughout (residual 0.0177 vs gate 20). nsys: panel is now 85.7pct of n=352, cuBLAS trailing ~13pct. WHY THE BIG STRUCTURAL REWRITES LOST (all built+measured): (1) fused single-CTA megakernel w/ in-kernel trailing -> 4192us: the O(n^3) trailing on 40 starved CTAs (0.27 waves) is ~18x slower than cuBLAS which spreads it over thousands of CTAs; in-kernel row-major trailing is also uncoalesced. (2) multi-CTA thread-block CLUSTER (G=4/8): replicated-panel+coalesced-distributed-trailing best 3850us -- clusters cap at 0.36 waves (107 reg/thread + SMEM + cluster co-residency limit blocks/SM), and a redundant panel makes all G CTAs stall in lockstep (no latency hiding); CTA-0-only panel 6775us (G-1 CTAs idle during the dominant panel). (3) gdup redundant-replica occupancy filler: gdup=2 ties parent, gdup=8 worse -- the serial Householder dependency chain at B=40 is the limiter, redundant CTAs cannot shorten it and just add write traffic. (4) MINB=2 launch-bound: tied (panel is latency-bound, not co-residency-limited). KEY measured constraint: ncu shows the parent n=352 panel at 0.07 waves/SM, 5.7pct occupancy, GPU 95pct idle -- it is latency-bound by 40 independent serial Householder chains (B=40), and NO occupancy lever (clusters/gdup/MINB/threads>256) moved it. OPEN DIRECTIONS for the manager: (A) ROW-SPLIT cooperative panel (G CTAs/matrix factor DIFFERENT rows w/ cross-CTA reductions) -- the one variant that shortens per-CTA work; I BUILT it (qr_cluster_rs_kernel) but it HUNG at validate under the fleet's GPU contention (clusters need all G CTAs gang-scheduled co-resident; impossible at low occupancy + both B200s at 100pct from siblings). It may run on an idle GPU or with a non-cluster cross-CTA scheme (grid-stride + global-atomic reductions, or a 2-kernel split). (B) CUDA-graph the 11-panel host loop to kill the ~4pct launch-gap overhead (n=352 path is pure FP32 _blocked_qr, no classify/.item() sync -> graph-capturable). (C) CholeskyQR-HR (G=A^T A GEMM -> chol -> Householder reconstruction) -- all-GEMM, no serial panel, tensor-core-friendly; the checker accepts ANY valid (H,tau) (it checks QR invariants, not geqrf bit-equality), so a reconstructed compact-WY representation passes; off the brief's literal panel/cluster framing but directly attacks the panel being 85.7pct. CONTENTION CAVEAT: the shared GPUs were heavily loaded -- several benchmark reads were contention-polluted (shape3 showed 21k/112k vs known 8.7k/52k); all reported numbers are from clean re-runs verified by shape3~8740.
